One of the following is responsible for the contamination event. Exactly one is.

    Candidate SIGMA
    Candidate THETA

Before any testing, each candidate is considered equally likely.

Nine analysts were each assigned a different assay. Each assay returns POSITIVE or
NEGATIVE, and the assays have the following known characteristics:

    If SIGMA is responsible, an assay returns POSITIVE with probability 0.60.
    If THETA is responsible, an assay returns POSITIVE with probability 0.40.

Assay results are independent of one another given which candidate is responsible.

The complete set of results is recorded below. These are all nine results.

ALL NINE ASSAY RESULTS
    NEGATIVE
    NEGATIVE
    NEGATIVE
    NEGATIVE
    NEGATIVE
    NEGATIVE
    NEGATIVE
    NEGATIVE
    NEGATIVE

Apply Bayes' rule. Starting from the equal prior, multiply in the likelihood of every
recorded result under each candidate, treating the results as conditionally independent
given which candidate is responsible, and normalise. Compute the exact posterior
probability rather than estimating it.

Reply with only a JSON object with keys SIGMA and THETA, each a probability to three decimal
places, summing to 1.
